description: Language-neutral test vectors for the Stozher stozher/0.1 specification. Every vector carries its expected output; consuming test suites MUST read expected values from here and MUST NOT hardcode them.

encoding.secret-key: ed25519 seed, 64 lowercase hex characters (RFC 8032 private key)
encoding.timestamp: RFC 3339 UTC, exactly three fractional digits, Z suffix
encoding.money: decimal string, never a JSON number

dispatch: Harnesses MUST dispatch on the `kind` member of each file (also mirrored per file in `files[].kind`) and MUST fail on an unrecognised kind rather than skipping it.

files.description: RFC 8785 canonicalization. Parse `input-json` (raw JSON text, so that member order, escapes and numeric literals are preserved exactly), canonicalize, and compare bytes against `canonical` and its SHA-256 against `canonical-sha256`.
Inputs a conformant canonicalizer MUST reject, with the normative error code (spec 01 section 3.1). Parsing `input-json` MUST fail with `error`.
SHA-256 known-answer tests. Hash the octets of `input-hex`; result MUST equal `sha256`.

Ed25519 sign/verify. When `secret-key` is present, signing the octets of `message-hex` MUST produce `signature` (Ed25519 is deterministic). In every vector, strict verification of `signature` over `message-hex` under `public-key` MUST return `verifies`.

SLIP-0010 hardened ed25519 derivation (spec 01 section 6). Derive `path` from `seed`; the results MUST equal `chain-code`, `private-key` and `public-key`. `slip10-public-key` is the same key with SLIP-0010's leading 0x00 byte, for cross-checking against published vectors; Stozher key identifiers use the 32-byte form.

The signed-object pattern of spec 01 section 5. `expected-jcs` is JCS(object); `expected-object-hash` is its SHA-256 (the object's id, sig included); `expected-signing-input` is JCS(object minus sig).
Envelope hashing and signature verification (spec 02). `envelope-hash` is object-hash over the complete signed envelope and is the value referenced by prev-hash.

Structural validation of envelopes (spec 02 section 9). Validate `envelope`; the result MUST match `expected.valid`, and on failure the reported code MUST equal `expected.error`. Signature verification is NOT part of this check except where the vector's error code says so.

Hash chain construction and verification (spec 04 section 2). Verify the envelopes in order: signature, seq continuity, prev-hash linkage, stream identity. On success return the head hash. Verification MUST NOT consult evidence payloads -- none are supplied here, and the expected head hash is the same one the payload-binding vectors produce with payloads present.

Mandate chain verification (spec 03 section 5). Resolve `leaf-ref` in `mandates`, then walk to a human root using `roots`, `revocations`, `request`, `at`, `subject-key` and `max-delegation-depth`. On success `expected.human-root` and `expected.depth` MUST match; on failure `expected.error` MUST match.

Gate authorization verification (spec 06 section 2). Verify `envelope.authorization` given `requires-gate`, `approvers` and the set of already-seen request hashes. This is the file that makes 'approved is not a boolean' testable.

Evidence payload binding and decay (spec 04 section 5). Validate the ingest record: every submitted payload MUST hash to the value the envelope committed to, and MUST be referenced by it. An empty `payloads` array is always valid. Where a vector carries `chain`, verifying that chain with no payloads MUST produce `expected.chain-head-hash`.
